mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 5% and 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases and 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO < 12-month MA and 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases, it signals a weak labor market, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS decreases, but 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with an increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) suggests a shift towards risk-off sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases and RSAFS increases, but 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) above its 12-month moving average signals strong economic growth, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 > 12-month MA and 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases and UNRATE increases, but 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
